1.1: 1.1 Argument. He writes to a holy woman so far that he does not hesitate to address her in the letter as lady, and bears witness to her children that they walk in the truth. Not I. About to write against heretics who have fallen from the truth, he says that of all who have known the truth there is one love toward the saints, so that by the likeness of Catholics he may deter from fellowship with heretics. For all the faithful agree in one truth, the heretics oppose one another in their errors.
1.4: 1.4 I rejoiced greatly. As if he said: What you hold, hold. Receive nothing else from heretics, because I rejoice in what you have; I desire nothing else to be added for your salvation. Since therefore I rejoice in your good beginning, do not make me grieve by your failure, because as a solicitous guardian I know all that is done about you. Walking in the truth. Adam was placed in paradise to work it and to keep it. Working signifies the effect of advancement: keeping, the state and constancy of perfection itself.
1.8: 1.8 Look to yourselves, etc. Do not consent to such, but rather attend how you may be perfectly instructed in faith and constancy. But that you may receive a full reward, that is, may take the true God with full joy, by persevering in the doctrine handed down to you, and not consenting to their error.
1.9: 1.9 And does not abide. If anyone separates himself from divine doctrine, so as to be outside right faith and the conduct of the commandments of God, he separates himself from God so as not to have God. Through the active and contemplative life, God becomes someone's by manifesting to him who is the Creator of all. He who abides. He abides in evangelical doctrine who thinks and acts according to it; he separates himself from it who thinks and acts otherwise.
1.10: 1.10 Nor say to him, Hail. Because it seems a sign of consent to the error, for we say this to friends whose works please us, and you, if perhaps you were not deceived, yet others through such familiarity of yours could be deceived, who would believe those please you, and so would believe them.
1.12: 1.12 Having many things. Understand that this admonition will be very useful to you, because for the confirmation of it I have also decided to come to you, nor yet could I in the meantime keep wholly silent.
1.13: 1.13 The children of your sister greet you. As he forbids saying Hail to the adversaries of the truth, so on the contrary he greets the elect in the person of the elect.
